title: Bounded walks give restricted reachability
statement: Let $E$ be a relation on the natural numbers, and let $n,j,c,t\in\mathbb{N}$ with $c<n$. If there is a walk from $c$ to $t$ of length at most $j$, in which each initial vertex of a step is less than $n$ and each step follows $E$, then $t$ is reachable from $c$ by a finite sequence of steps whose endpoints are both less than $n$ and whose steps follow $E$. A walk of length at most $j$ is defined recursively: at bound zero it means $c=t$, and at a positive bound it means either $c=t$ or there is $v<n$ with $E(c,v)$ and a walk of length at most $j-1$ from $v$ to $t$.
hypotheses_covered: there is a bounded walk from $c$ to $t$
